title: Bill Simmons Suggests Blockbuster Nikola Jokic Trade to Rockets
text:
Bill Simmons Suggests Blockbuster Nikola Jokic Trade to Rockets - BasketballNews NBA Play Hoops Rank NBA Play Hoops Rank Home / NBA Bill Simmons Suggests Blockbuster Nikola Jokic Trade to Rockets
 By
 Ubong Richard Nov 18, 2026, 4:09 PM CUT
 Imago
 Denver Nuggets at Orlando Magic, Orlando, Florida, USA Orlando, Florida, USA, December 27, 2025, Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic 15 at the Kia Center. Copyright: xMartyxJean-Louisx
 Howard Beck wrote this month that every rival executive is monitoring the Nuggets’ struggles. Bill Simmons has now turned that idea into a specific proposal: Houston should make one call for Nikola Jokic.
 Simmons floated the idea on his podcast, framing it as a possible solution to a Rockets team that lacks size and paint scoring.
 “Do they just make one play for Joker and just see what Denver says? Because they can put Sengun in that trade, they can put Sheppard, they can put Capela’s expiring, they could put those swap picks they have, the Phoenix first. They could just say, screw it, we’re going for the Sengun to Joker upgrade. We’re gonna put Joker on this team and he solves every problem we have… Offensively we become a terror,” Simmons said .
 Simmons also offered fallback options. "Do they think about going after Jamal Murray instead, with VanVleet and some contracts and a pick, and just try to upgrade a point guard? Do they try to figure out Anthony Davis, which I think KD would have to be involved? These are all things I'm sure they're talking about." Murray earns $50.1 million, and Fred VanVleet earns $25.0 million.
 The package Simmons described is built around players Houston would give up. Alperen Sengun is paid $35.6 million, Reed Sheppard $11.1 million and Clint Capela $7.0 million, and sending all three would create $53.7 million in cap space to absorb Jokic's salary. 
 Sengun currently leads Houston with 22.8 points and 9.3 rebounds per game. Giving him up would be costly, which is the point of Simmons’ “upgrade” language.
 There is no indication Denver has made Jokic available. Jokic will be eligible next summer to sign a five-year, $359.5 million deal that could include a no-trade clause, and it will be interesting to see if Denver offers it, given the team’s struggles this season and a decline in his numbers compared to previous years.
 Given Jokic's position in Denver, even Simmons' package might not be enough, and the Rockets may have a better shot at landing Anthony Davis. Davis' desire to play for a contender doesn't align with Washington's 4-11 record. Simmons himself said Kevin Durant would have to be involved in a Davis deal, so any version of the trade would still cost Houston a star.
 The Murray option is more modest but has its own issues. Simmons described it as a point guard upgrade and suggested using VanVleet, other contracts and a pick.
 Jokic’s situation in Denver is what gives the idea traction. Beck reported that Jokic “sounds a little testy,” though Beck himself asked whether it was “comically premature” to speculate.
 Analysts note that Houston would give up a lot, Denver has no reason to listen, and Davis looks easier to get than Jokic.
 A trade involving the three-time MVP would be one of the biggest in league history, and no outlet has reported any contact between the teams. For now, it is a podcast pitch.
